newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Dutch doubt Lisbon will make EMU in 1999 -paper.
newsitem.headline: Dutch doubt Lisbon will make EMU in 1999 -paper.

text.p: Dutch Finance Minister Gerrit Zalm said that he doubted that Portugal would be amongst European Union countries to launch the single currency in 1999, the Diario Economico reported on Tuesday.

The newspaper said that it had asked the minister, who will chair meetings of EU finance ministers for the next six months, about Lisbon's chances of qualifying in the first wave of countries for Economic and Monetary Union (EMU).
Although he believed that Portugal was "objectively better placed than Spain," Zalm said that he had serious doubts that the escudo could be included from the start of EMU, the newspaper reported.

Zalm gave a briefing for Brussels-based journalists in the Hague on Monday at which he said that a lot of EU states would be wise to take some time in qualifying for monetary union in order to make sure they were able to sustain low budget deficits.
He said that EMU would probably "start with a smaller group of countries".
Portugal has made qualifying for EMU its top policy priority and its 1997 budget plan calls for a deficit of 2.9 percent of Gross Domestic Product (GDP), inside the three percent EMU ceiling.
